verdict.rationale: Smithery's service tokens let you scope an agent's access to specific connections, using a namespace plus a metadata filter, so it can list and call tools only on those connections. That gives server-level restriction. There is no evidence of per-tool allowlists or blocking individual tools within a connection. missing for 10: per-tool allow/deny controls, explicit allowlist configuration documentation, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can restrict which servers and individual tools an agent may call through allowlists or per-tool access control

citations.quote: This token can list and call tools on connections in `my-app` where `metadata.userId` is `user-123` — nothing else.
Service tokens let you safely expose Smithery to browsers, mobile apps, and AI agents without leaking your API key.
